title: Metals data table and choices sheet
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Metals and their uses (8G); energy transfers (8K)
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 43 (Metals data table and choices sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 43: Metal properties and uses. To understand how the properties of metals decide what each metal is used for

questions.q: Why are saucepan bases often copper?
questions.a: Copper is an excellent thermal conductor, so heat spreads quickly
questions.model: What does a pan base need to do? Pass heat from the hob to the food. Which property? Good thermal conductor. Copper is one of the best.

questions.q: Which property lets copper be made into wires?
Why are overhead power cables aluminium, not copper?
questions.a: Aluminium is much less dense (lighter) and cheaper

questions.q: Use the data table on the sheet (density, strength, conductivity, cost, corrosion) to choose a metal for four jobs and justify each.
questions.a: Sensible choices with data, e.g. bike frame: aluminium (light, strong enough, no rust)
questions.model: Teacher does the first: 'electrical wire: copper, because the table shows the highest conductivity at a reasonable cost'.

questions.q: Explain why gold is used in phones even though it is expensive.
questions.a: Excellent conductor, does not corrode; only tiny amounts needed

questions.q: Suggest why titanium is used for hip replacements.
questions.a: Strong, low density, does not corrode or react in the body

questions.q: Big question: why is gold in mobile phones?
questions.a: It conducts very well and never corrodes.
